reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both semantic grounding and statistical validation of shared spurious features, especially since the ground truth is unknown and the model may rely on noise or spurious signals. The combination improves robustness in identifying features that are present in all misclassified cases but lack semantic relevance to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify all features that appear in both instance 13590 and instance 31054, and determine which features are shared across all misclassified instances (if more were available)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared feature names (e.g., education-num, marital-status, occupation, relationship) that appear in every misclassified instance

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate if any shared feature (e.g., education-num=9, age) has a semantically plausible link to income level, or if it is an outlier in terms of feature distribution relative to the correct class
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification that the shared features are not semantically meaningful or are correlated with the ground truth due to spurious patterns

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a robust, globally consistent attribution measure across instances, allowing us to identify features with high impact in misclassified cases, especially when applied in intersection mode to focus on shared high-importance features. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability and gradient-based attribution, respectively, which help detect spurious feature influence. Sensitivity analysis isolates whether feature removal changes predictions, confirming spuriousness. Together, they validate the autonomy-driven hypotheses with empirical evidence from the model's behavior.
